title: PNP reminds gamers not to imitate crimes in real life amid GTA 6 release
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Friday reminded video game enthusiasts not to imitate criminal activities and violence depicted in video games following the release of Grand Theft Auto VI…

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Friday reminded video game enthusiasts not to imitate criminal activities and violence depicted in video games amid the release of a "highly anticipated" game.
In a statement, PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. pointed out the importance of distinguishing between digital entertainment and real-world conduct.

“Entertainment must never blur our understanding of right and wrong. What may be permissible in a virtual world has no place in real life when it violates the law, endangers others, or disregards human life,” Nartatez said.

While the PNP did not identify any specific game, the statement comes amid the release of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) which prompted police departments in the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia to remind players against imitating criminal activities depicted in virtual settings.
After 13 years of anticipation and an estimated production cost of at least $1 billion, the highly anticipated video game GTA 6 has finally been released, Reuters reported on Thursday.
The latest installment in the blockbuster video game franchise became available in New Zealand at midnight on Thursday, with its global rollout following different time zones.
Since its debut in 1997, GTA has grown into one of the best-selling video game series of all time, building a massive global following over nearly three decades, according to the report.
The PNP chief, meanwhile, reminded the public that acts of violence has "real world consequences."

“Every act of violence in the real world has consequences that cannot be reversed by a reset button or a respawn. We must strengthen awareness among our youth that firearms are not toys, violence is never a solution, and protecting human life must always come first,” he said.
Nartatez urged young Filipinos to exercise sound judgment both online and offline when exposed to content depicting violence and unlawful behavior.

“Enjoy your games but never allow fiction to dictate your actions in reality. Be responsible digital citizens, respect the rule of law, and remember that real-life choices carry real-life consequences,” he said. —VAL, GMA News
